newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Citybus to buy HK$380 mln in new buses by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Citybus to buy HK$380 mln in new buses by 1998.

text.p: Citybus Group Ltd will buy at least 180 new buses at a cost of about HK$380 million by April 1998 in a move to support the company's expansion, managing director Lyndon Ress said on Monday.

"We see organic growth in the public transport sector in Hong Kong. Such capital expenditure not only reflects our commitment to the long term but is also necessary for meeting customers' rising expectations," Ress told reporters.
The company said the buses would be used to support service to Hong Kong's new airport at Chep Lak Kok and to meet growing demand in Hong Kong and into China after 1997.
Ress said the new buses would be acquired through an open tender but gave no date or other details.
The purchase will be funded by the proceeds from a share issue, internal resources and bank borrowings, the company said.
The bus operator, a unit of CNT Group Ltd, is offering 250 million shares at HK$1.42 per share to raise capital funding for its expansion plans.
It said about HK$200 million would be used to develop its new airport franchised bus services and the balance would be used to repay bank borrowing and for working capital.
Samuel Cheng, a Citybus director, said the company's debt ratio would be reduced to 56 percent following the issue from 74 percent.
Trading in the shares is expected to begin on November 29.
Ress said he was optimistic over the group's future earnings due to growing demand for bus services in the British territory.
